newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to up foreign shr holding limit soon - report.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to up foreign shr holding limit soon - report.

text.p: South Korea's finance and economy ministry will soon announce the expansion of the foreign stock ownership ceiling, a Seoul newspaper on Wednesday quoted a senior finance and economy ministry official as saying.
South Korea has said it will expand the limit to 23 percent sometime this year from the current 20 percent.

"The announcement is imminent," the Naeway Economic Daily quoted Yoon Jeung-hyun, deputy minister for the financial policy devision, as saying. Yoon said the expansion would be used to help boost the market.
Yoon was not immediately available for comment.
Yoon also said the government was considering raising the ceiling to between 25 and 26 percent this year, instead of 23 percent, according to the newspaper report.
Helped by the newspaper report, the main Seoul stock index rose 2.54 percent to 655.14 in mid-afternoon trading. It rose 3.51 percent on Tuesday after falling for six previous trading days.
Finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said in an interview with the newspaper that he had delegated the decision on the foreign share ownership to working level officials.
